name: BirthDeath
title: The birth–death distribution on time trees

args.name: lambda
args.description: The speciation rate per lineage, in inverse units of tree age

args.name: mu
args.description: The extinction rate per lineage, in the same units as lambda

args.name: rho
args.description: The probability that a present-day lineage is sampled

args.name: age
args.description: AtAge(t), or Flat with Origin and Tips(n)

description:
A tree model with constant speciation and extinction rates. Returns the reconstructed tree on the supplied taxa, with tips at age zero and extinct lineages integrated out. Each present-day lineage is independently sampled with probability rho. Setting mu to zero and rho to one gives Yule.

Origin starts with one lineage; Crown fixes the root at the supplied starting age and requires sampled descendants from both initial lineages. Tips(n) conditions on the number of sampled taxa; Unconditioned retains its probability as evidence about the rates and starting age. Surviving conditions an Origin start on leaving sampled descendants and adds no condition to Crown.

Origin with Flat and Tips(n) integrates over a flat origin-age measure before conditioning on n. Other Flat combinations are not supported. Origin permits one taxon; Crown requires at least two.

Temporarily, sampling always generates a tree conditional on the supplied taxon count. Without Tips(n), this is an MCMC initializer rather than direct simulation of the declared law, and the tree variable must not be created or destroyed during MCMC.
